transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Lu (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (SignalForge Head of ML), Derek Cho (SignalForge Platform), Priya Nair (SignalForge Finance)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Redwood kickoff for a 6-week POC focused on unit economics for SignalForge's chat/assist feature. Main goals: agree success criteria (latency, cost per 100k tokens, quality regression bounds), gather workload traces, and schedule benchmark window. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated and caching/batching knobs. Next steps: SOW, benchmark schedule, cost-model spread.

Topics (auto-detected):
- Success criteria & timelines
- Workload sizing and traces
- Per-token cost estimates and batching impact
- Benchmark plan: seq len, prompt mix, eval metrics
- Security docs & deployment mode

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intros — i'm samira, AE on this account, and with me is evan, our solutions engineer.
[00:22] Marta: hi hi, i'm marta, i run the ML team at signalforge. we're trying to get a clean run at cost before we commit to a prod rollout.
[00:34] Derek: derek here, platform eng, i'll own infra bits and the benchmark runner.
[00:40] Priya: priya from finance — i'll be watching budget and approvals.
[00:46] Evan: great, high level goal for today's scoping is to walk through success criteria, workload sizing, and how we estimate per-token econ with batching and caching knobs, and then lock a benchmark window.
[01:05] Marta: perfect. to set context: we have a chat assistant, avg user session ~6 turns, avg tokens per request ~320 tokens (we think), 80% of traffic is short form Q&A and 20% has long contexts (documents). target latency P95 under 350ms for user interactive flows.
[01:30] Derek: our current infra is k8s with a mix of GCP gpu nodes and an on-prem pool. we prefer private deployment but can evaluate hosted for the pilot if cost/pricing makes sense.
[01:45] Samira: thanks — that's helpful. quick question for finance: what's an acceptable per-user monthly cost or total pilot budget?
[01:53] Priya: we have a runway for a six-week pilot of up to $45k excluding engineering time, but long term we need per-million-token budgeting to look reasonable versus our current CPU-based baseline.
[02:10] Evan: ok noted. i'm going to talk through the cost model we typically use — it's tokenized cost + infra amortized + caching savings. sample back-of-envelope: for a 13B quantized model on A100-ish equivalent with our batching and prefix cache, we often see $8–$12 per 1M input+output tokens for interactive latency targets; with aggressive batching that can drop to $4–$6 per 1M but at higher p95.
[02:40] Marta: can you repeat that? the numbers feel lower than we expected, did you include infra and license?
[02:46] Evan: yes, that's a host-side, includes reserved capacity amortization example and basic ops. it assumes some caching — prefix KV cache — and a mix of 70/30 host/dedicated cases. i should caveat model variant matters a lot.
[03:05] Samira: also important: our routing can fall back to cheaper quantized variants when latency slack exists; we can show iso-quality configs.
[03:18] Derek: how do you measure quality? our bar is <1.5% regression on rouge/accuracy on our eval set.
[03:26] Evan: good call — we'll need your eval prompts. we'll run the bench with the same eval harness and track hels like rouge, exact match, and human spot-checks. 
[03:40] Marta: there's some noise in our current request distribution. we'll provide a 7-day trace with token counts and percentiles. expect a fat tail — spikes during batch jobs.
[03:52] Evan: perfect. for the bench we want a 48-hour run that includes ramp and steady-state. Derek, can you expose a test endpoint or we can run against hosted?
[04:04] Derek: either is fine. on-prem team's fine, but network egress and firewall rules might take 24h to approve.
[04:14] Samira: ok we'll plan the benchmark for a ~48 hour window starting after you give traces; evan will schedule.
[04:22] Evan: on batching knobs — two levers: dynamic batching (pack multiple requests into one forward) and micro-batching (short delays to increase batch depth). dynamic batching is low-latency friendly and depends on request arrival patterns. micro-batching trades a bit of added ms for much lower cost per token.
[04:40] Marta: can you give an example tradeoff?
[04:43] Evan: sure, rough example: without batching, p50 token cost might be X; with 20–30ms micro-batch window we often reduce CPU/GPU utilization per-token by ~30% which can cut per-1M-token cost from $10 to $6 in our examples. however p95 latency can increase by 40–80ms depending on arrival.
[05:07] Priya: finance question — are these unit figures normalized per model-size? we want a per-100k-token number for budgeting.
[05:15] Evan: yes we'll convert everything to per-100k and per-1M in the spreadsheet we share. we also include sensitivity rows: batch window 0/10/30/50ms, cache hit rates 0/25/50/75%.
[05:29] Marta: let's talk about cache — we have many repeated prefixes in session flows. how does prefix caching interact with our conversational cache?
[05:36] Evan: our prefix/KV cache stores repeated prefix key/value states and avoids re-computing them each request. if you have 40% hit rate on prefixes you can see dramatic token compute savings. for example with a 40% KV hit rate plus safe batching you'll cut total compute tokens by ~30%. note: cache hit measurement is imperfect, so we'll need sample traces.
[06:01] Derek: what about stateful sessions and eviction policies? we need TTLs and memory planning.
[06:08] Evan: yes we model cache eviction by LRU with configurable TTL, and we estimate memory footprint per model and per-ttl. we'll include those estimates in the SOW.
[06:20] Marta: what about model quantization and quality tradeoffs? we can't accept big quality drops.
[06:26] Evan: we recommended testing a 8-bit quant variant as a fallback; typically quality drop is small for many open models but must be validated against your eval set. Redwood Optimize suggests candidates with minimal quality regression.
[06:42] Samira: and our smart routing can prefer accuracy-first variants for high-value users and cheaper variants for bulk autocompletions.
[06:49] Priya: timeline: if we start next week, when's delivery for a 48-hour benchmark?
[06:55] Samira: dependent on traces and firewall but we estimate: traces day 0, bench prep 2 days, benchmark window day 3–4. so earliest bench mid next week.
[07:05] Marta: quality metrics again — we want p95 latency <350ms, per-1M-token cost target < $7 if possible, and quality regression <1.5% as mentioned. those are our success criteria.
[07:18] Evan: noted. we'll aim to produce a guardrail matrix: cost vs latency vs quality.
[07:24] Derek: can you include a Dedicated capacity example? our legal prefers dedicated for PII workloads.
[07:30] Samira: yes, we'll include both Dedicated and Hosted in the SOW. Dedicated has higher fixed amortized cost but predictable throughput and isolation; we'll show how longer term it scales on per-token.
[07:45] Evan: also mentioning network egress and KMS -- for private you'll need KMS integration and we can show HSM/KMS patterns. security pack will be in the docs.
[07:56] Priya: legal will want retention and audit logs — is that part of Redwood Private?
[08:02] Samira: yes audit logs and retention controls are in our Private offering; we'll include a doc link.
[08:08] Marta: how do you handle model rollbacks if a new quant rollout causes regressions?
[08:12] Evan: rollouts are canary based; we have automatic fallback policies and traffic splitting. we'll propose a rollback SLA in the SOW.
[08:21] Derek: benchmark specifics — sequence lengths? we need to capture short queries and long doc embeddings.
[08:27] Evan: we'll do a mix: seq len buckets: 64, 256, 512, 1024. for the chat flows use mixed-turn sequences to emulate session context. also include a small set of long context re-runs to exercise KV cache.
[08:40] Marta: are you going to simulate user think time? that affects batching.
[08:44] Evan: yes, arrival distribution will be modeled from your traces; we'll run a synthetic traffic generator plus real traces playback.
[08:50] Samira: ok, let's lock responsibilities: Derek provides traces and test endpoint; Marta provides eval prompts and quality thresholds; Priya shares budget cadence; Evan will seed the cost model and schedule bench; Samira will produce SOW and security pack.
[09:06] Priya: if the numbers show >$10 per 1M at our latency requirement we'll need to evaluate a hybrid approach and probable feature gating.
[09:15] Evan: understood. the spreadsheet will include thresholds and sensitivity so you can see where the breakpoint is.
[09:22] Marta: any competitor or self-host concern we should call out? our infra team looked at Replicate but it lacked the batching and cache controls we need.
[09:32] Samira: correct, major cloud offerings have different tradeoffs — we'll include a short competitive note.
[09:37] Derek: how long is POC duration? you mentioned six weeks earlier.
[09:40] Samira: typical POC is 4–6 weeks: week 0 onboarding and traces, week 1 bench & analysis, week 2 optimization, week 3 final report and pilot SOW. we can compress based on priorities.
[09:54] Marta: can you share a sample cost per 100k token now? rough ballpark?
[09:58] Evan: ballpark for a 13B on a cost-optimized host: $0.8–$1.2 per 100k tokens with batching/cache assumptions; without batching and no cache it's closer to $2.0–$2.5 per 100k. again highly workload-dependent.
[10:18] Priya: good to have those numbers. will you show how reserved vs on-demand affects that?
[10:22] Evan: yes the sheet will include reserved/spot/dedicated scenarios.
[10:26] Marta: follow-up — do you have standard ev test harness or do we need to build one?
[10:30] Evan: we have a harness and we can integrate your eval prompts. we prefer to run with your traces for highest fidelity.
[10:36] Derek: anything else on infra metrics? we need memory, vram, and network estimates per model.
[10:41] Evan: we'll include model memory footprints, kv cache memory, and per-GPU throughput curves.
[10:46] Marta: can Redwood run the benchmark in our env? gives better fidelity.
[10:49] Samira: yes we can run in your private env — we'll need firewall access and an admin user; Derek said that's feasible but may take 24h.
[10:58] Priya: question on cost split: do you show cost-of-goods vs margin so we can model economics?
[11:03] Evan: the sheet will show gross per-token cost and suggested pass-through markup rows so finance can model unit economics.
[11:10] Marta: any caveats we should be aware of?
[11:12] Evan: tokenization differences across models can affect per-token accounting; we'll normalize to tkn counts using your tokenizer. also mis-transcriptions here: KV cache sometimes shows as KV cash in earlier notes, ignore that — just a transcript quirk.
[11:25] Derek: haha noted.
[11:28] Samira: let's talk concrete next steps and dates.
[11:32] Evan: i'll take the cost-model action and seed the spreadsheet today. samira will send SOW draft by friday. derek please share traces by wednesday. marta confirm eval set by thursday. priya confirm budget cadence by next monday.
[11:50] Marta: ok sounds good. one more thing — do you provide optimization suggestions after bench?
[11:55] Evan: yes, Redwood Optimize will produce recommendations: micro-batching windows, quant profiles, candidate model variants, and cache TTL tuning. we include estimated cost delta per recommendation.
[12:06] Priya: if this goes well and we can get under $7 per 1M tokens at p95 <350ms and quality delta <1.5% we can move to a 12-month reserved capacity discussion.
[12:18] Samira: perfect, that's a clear buy-signal. we'll aim for that target.
[12:23] Derek: any dependencies on our side beyond traces and endpoint?
[12:26] Derek: firewall approvals and an account owner for test creds.
[12:30] Samira: we'll include a checklist in the SOW.
[12:33] Evan: i'll also include a suggested traffic pattern for the bench (ramp up 10m, 60m steady state, sawtooth spikes to simulate traffic).
[12:43] Marta: timeline recap?
[12:46] Samira: Derek traces by 2027-03-03, Evan cost model by 2027-03-04, Samira SOW by 2027-03-05, bench 48-hour window mid next week, follow-up meeting after bench.
[12:59] Priya: ok that's good, i'll await the SOW and cost sheet.
[13:05] Samira: thanks everyone. quick recap of deliverables and owners in the email i'll send. appreciate it.
[13:12] Marta: thanks all.
[13:15] Meeting end.

- Bench plan: 48-hour run with seq len buckets 64/256/512/1024, synthetic + trace playback

- Next steps and owners captured in action_items list above
